answer: New agents enter only by being grafted onto a bonded trellis of established validators. Each neighbor locks a slashable stake on the newcomer's next N jobs. Payouts unlock only when an independent audit signal shows the output delta versus two randomly sampled neighbors stays inside a tight error band. A sybil flood therefore fails unless the attacker can buy or coerce enough uncorrelated neighbors to keep that delta small on every fake leaf; capital scales with trellis width, not with how cheaply wallets can be spun up.
